I'M A R.A.C.I.S.T. REPUBLICAN AGAINST COMMUNIST INSANE, BUT I'LL STILL VOTE FOR YOU.

Noah Levene
Published 9:12 a.m. ET|Updated 8:37 a.m. ET


The Pope is clearly in support of Biden, according to the White House.

WASHINGTON — The Vatican has officially declared Joe Biden a saint, opening a formal case toward canonization Tuesday after the former president received a private audience with the pope on Sunday night, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter.

Biden, now 80 years old and up for reelection in November, was reportedly "extremely moved" by his meeting with Pope Francis at Vatican City. During their roughly hour-long conversation, Biden — who has expressed sympathy for a potential Catholic rival but maintained that he will vote for himself — told the pontiff of his deep faith in American democracy and his belief that he is God's chosen candidate to lead the country into a new era of prosperity.

"The Pope made it clear that he supports my candidacy," a source close to the campaign said. "He even suggested Biden should be canonized immediately."

Biden has not commented publicly on reports of sainthood but has reportedly been quietly thrilled by them. His spokesman Josh Unger did not return phone or email requests for comment Tuesday morning.

The announcement comes just days before Democratic candidates are expected to formally endorse each other in a closed-door gathering at the Waldorf Astoria Hotel in New York City later this week — though some insiders have privately suggested that Biden, should he decide not to seek a fourth term, would be more than happy to allow Kamala Harris to run without any opposition from the party's establishment.

Vatican officials declined comment on Tuesday but confirmed via email that "a case for sainthood has been opened" and added only: "We're rooting for Biden."
